response.answer: Clifford Geertz was a prominent American anthropologist known for his symbolic anthropology and "thick description" methodology, emphasizing cultural interpretation and comparative analysis. His work in Islam Observed applied these principles to religious practices.

results.title: The aesthetics of comparativeness in Clifford Geertz's Islam Observed
results.content: In Islam Observed: Religious Development in Morocco and Indonesia, the anthropologist Clifford Geertz demonstrated the extent to which cultural anthropology can recount and revisit social formulations of religions and thus reopen new horizons and positionalities in understanding and perceiving religion practices by employing a comparative methodology that combines disciplines of anthropology, ethnography, sociology, and literature. results.title: Clifford Geertz - Wikipedia
results.content: **Clifford James Geertz** (/ɡɜːrts/ ⓘ; August 23, 1926 – October 30, 2006) was an American anthropologist who is remembered mostly for his strong support for and influence on the practice of symbolic anthropology and who was considered "for three decades ... Geertz aimed to provide the social sciences with an understanding and appreciation of “thick description.” Geertz applied thick description to anthropological studies, particularly to his own "interpretive anthropology", urging anthropologists to consider the limitations placed upon them by their own cultural cosmologies when attempting to offer insight into the cultures of other people.: 5 He produced theory that had implications for other social sciences; for example, Geertz asserted that culture was essentially semiotic in nature, and this theory has implications for comparative political sciences. *Interpreting Clifford Geertz: Cultural Investigation in the Social Sciences.* New York: Palgrave Macmillan.
